Fixes motors remaining stationary in Cleanup and Learn Powder, plus control-loop
and firmware-update defects.

| File | Board |
|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.22-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) |
| `opentrickler-v2.22-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) |

Install this update using **USB BOOTSEL**. Earlier firmware has board-specific
OTA defects that this update cannot correct until it is installed. Use only the
UF2 matching your board.

## Motor startup

The PIO resource allocator loaded the stepper program and claimed state machines,
but never initialized or enabled those state machines. Motor commands reached
the queues without producing STEP pulses. Each motor now initializes its STEP
pin and state machine, starts at zero speed, and enables the state machine.

The motor queues also allocated 12-byte items while sending and receiving
4-byte floats, allowing stack corruption. Their item size now matches the data.

## Control and calibration

- Stop commands avoid division by zero and invalid float-to-integer conversions.
- Motor and servo ramps handle microsecond timer rollover; unchanged motor speeds
  do not divide by a zero-length ramp duration.
- PID derivatives handle samples arriving in the same RTOS tick.
- Charge, top-up, and timed Learn runs stop after two seconds without a finite
  scale reading. Cancel during charging explicitly stops both motors.
- Learn opens an enabled servo gate before timed calibration and closes it on exit.
  Disabled gates remain unused.

## Firmware updates

- OTA staging and image capacity use the board's actual flash size.
- Pico W validation reads the vector table after its 256-byte bootloader.
- The portal checks board family, UF2 payload sizes, overlapping blocks, and update
  capacity; it checks whether the apply request succeeds.
- Concurrent and oversized uploads are rejected, and connection cleanup preserves
  the active upload. Failure to create the apply task is reported.

## Validation and compatibility

Both board variants passed local Debug builds and picotool image checks. Ten host
regression groups passed, including motor initialization, worker commands, timer
rollover, scale timeout, and OTA parsing. Hardware/RTOS calls are mocked in the host
tests; physical motor movement, flashing, OTA execution, and charge accuracy still
require hardware validation.

No EEPROM layout, acceptance bracket, or tuning-default changes. Existing settings
and profiles carry over. This release does not claim an 8–9 second throw time.
